summary: SDK single-connection stall + chained retries causing elevated client-side latency and perceived timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent but sustained increases in end-to-end request latency (and occasional client-side timeouts) starting 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC. Impact: User-facing document generation API calls slow from median ~120ms to 2-6s; some requests hit client-side 5s timeout. Environment: NimbleDocs Dedicated account on prod-us-east, SDK v1.4.2 (Python), app using default client config with connection_pool_size=1 and retry/backoff enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a steady concurrent workload of ~20 clients producing requests at ~4 qps each using SDK v1.4.2 and default config. 2) Observe request latencies and number of retries from SDK logs. 3) Compare with same workload using connection_pool_size=8 or http2 multiplexing. Observed behavior: Long-tail latency spike and a pattern of serialized request retries: when a single underlying TCP connection stalls (socket in CLOSE_WAIT or waiting on TLS handshake), multiple SDK requests queue behind it; retries are attempted in sequence with exponential backoff but no jitter, producing retry chains that amplify head-of-line blocking. Expected behavior: SDK should maintain parallelism and avoid large serialized retry chains; backoff should include jitter and pool should allow more than one in-flight connection to upstream. Logs/traces: "[2026-03-10T10:14:21Z] sdk.request: attempt=1 request_id=abc123 waiting for connection (pool-size=1)"; "[2026-03-10T10:14:24Z] sdk.request: attempt=2 request_id=abc123 retrying after backoff=1000ms"; Upstream gateway shows healthy 2xx responses for the same time window. Attachments: customer supplied SDK debug logs and pcap showing repeated TCP retransmits.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:02 - Maya Patel (Support): Received initial report from NimbleDocs CS. Customer provided SDK debug logs and a short pcap. Noted SDK config: connection_pool_size=1, max_retries=4, backoff_base_ms=200, jitter=0.

2026-03-10 11:25 - NimbleDocs Engineering (customer): We rolled a small change on our side yesterday but traffic pattern is similar. We haven't changed SDK config intentionally. Observed timeouts on ~3% of requests during peak.

2026-03-10 12:10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Investigating. Checked api-gateway and serving-runtime dashboards. No spike in 5xx or CPU on serving nodes. Connection logs show transient TLS handshake delays from a few client IPs. Hypothesis: client-side pool of 1 plus aggressive retry/backoff without jitter results in serialized retries and perceived timeouts.
2026-03-10 13:00 - Support (Maya): Suggested immediate mitigation: set connection_pool_size=8 and enable jitter in backoff. Requested customer to test changes in staging and to run a short A/B test.
2026-03-10 13:45 - NimbleDocs (customer): Applied config changes in staging and saw median latency return to ~140ms and tail latencies reduced. Will push to prod in 30 minutes.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Follow-up: After prod deploy, customer's telemetry shows stabilized latencies. Collected and attached additional traces. Creating SDK bug/feature request for safer defaults and clearer docs.
2026-03-12 08:55 - Maya Patel (Support): Closing note to customer with recommended permanent fixes and link to PR; confirmed customer is satisfied and ticket marked resolved.
investigation_notes: Checked platform metrics: no correlated increase in server-side queuing or error rates. Gateway logs show steady 2xx rate for NimbleDocs's API key during incident window.

Reproduced locally with a test harness: single TCP connection + induced 200-400ms TLS delay on connect produced serialized SDK request queues and exponential retry chains that caused many client requests to exceed a 5s client timeout.
Identified config pattern: connection_pool_size=1 + max_retries>0 + backoff with no jitter produces deterministic retry alignment across concurrent callers, amplifying head-of-line blocking.
Verified workaround: increasing pool size to 4-8 or enabling HTTP/2 multiplexing eliminates queueing; adding randomized jitter to backoff reduces synchronized retries and long tails.
Raised SDK ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/623 (request default pool_size=8, enable jitter, and document recommended production config).
resolution: Applied recommended mitigation with customer: increase SDK connection_pool_size to 8 and enable exponential backoff with full jitter. Customer rolled change to prod and tail latency returned to baseline within 15 minutes. Action items closed: 1) SDK team accepted the issue and opened PR to change defaults and improve docs (PR #482). 2) Support updated runbook to include 'pool_size >= min(8, CPU_cores*2) or use HTTP/2' guidance and to call out jitter. 3) Engineering to add a health check in SDK that warns when pool_size==1 with retries enabled. Customer confirmed successful recovery and ticket resolved.
postmortem_action_items: SDK: default pool_size increased and jitter enabled by default (PR merged)
Support: update Troubleshooting KB with 'serialized retry' checklist
SRE: add dashboard alert for unusually high client-side retry rates linked to customer API keys
Customer: review SDK upgrade plan and remove legacy config overrides
